messages:
maria-dev: Heads up — running our JS SDK tests in Vitest + edge adapter and hitting a bunch of ESM/CJS + mocking failures. Happening locally and in CI. Anyone run into this?

josh: Can you paste the error you see?

maria-dev: Minimal repro error: 
```
Error: SyntaxError: Cannot use import statement outside a module
    at Object.Module._extensions..js (internal/modules/cjs/loader.js:123)
    at Module.load (internal/modules/cjs/loader.js:103)
    at tryModuleLoad (internal/modules/cjs/loader.js:62)
...
```
It's coming from node_modules/@redwood-inference/sdk/dist/esm/index.js when Vitest tries to run tests. Also mocks don't seem to apply to named exports (createClient).

alex: Are you on Vitest or Jest for these tests? Edge adapter changes runtime semantics sometimes.

maria-dev: Vitest locally, but our CI runs Jest for legacy suites. Both are flaky. Vitest config already has `environment: 'edge'` for the adapter.

samir: Common pain: package is published with ESM-only entrypoints, test runners default to CJS or use transformIgnorePatterns which skip node_modules. Two approaches: 1) make SDK publish a CJS wrapper/top-level main, or 2) make test runner transform the ESM files.

josh: Can you share your vitest.config?

maria-dev: snippet: 
```js
import { defineConfig } from 'vitest/config'
export default defineConfig({
  test: {
    environment: 'happy-dom',
    globals: true,
    // tried adding deps.inline but still failing
    // deps: { inline: ['@redwood-inference/sdk'] },
  }
})
```
Error shows: `Unexpected token 'export' in node_modules/@redwood-inference/sdk/dist/esm/index.js` after adding inline deps it shifted but didn't resolve mock issues.

alex: For Vitest try `deps: { inline: ['@redwood-inference/sdk'] }` plus a `resolve.alias` to a test-mock file. For Jest you often need `transformIgnorePatterns` to allow transforming the package, e.g. 
```json
"transformIgnorePatterns": ["/node_modules/(?!@redwood-inference/sdk)"]
```
But Jest may still choke on native ESM unless you opt into `--experimental-vm-modules` for Node 18.

samir: Another practical SDK-side fix: add an exports map and include both import and require entrypoints: 
```json
"exports": {
  ".": { "import": "./dist/esm/index.js", "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js" }
}
```
And publish a small CJS build at dist/cjs that re-exports. That gives consumers tests and old Node callers something to require.

katy: FYI our published package currently has an `exports` map but some deep imports (like `@redwood-inference/sdk/lib/something`) point only at esm files. Tests that deep-import can still hit ESM-only paths. We should either discourage deep imports or add CJS shims for those paths.

maria-dev: Workaround I tried for Vitest: alias the SDK to a test shim: 
```js
resolve: {
  alias: {
    '@redwood-inference/sdk': path.resolve(__dirname, 'test/__mocks__/sdk-cjs.js')
  }
}
```
That made mocking reliable locally. But Jest in CI still fails — mocks do not attach because Jest resolves to the published ESM entry.

josh: For Jest you can also create a manual mock inside `__mocks__` that matches the package name and ensure `jest.mock('@redwood-inference/sdk')` picks it up. If Jest still loads ESM before mock, then transform config is the root cause.

samir: Another trick: publish a tiny cjs wrapper at package root: `index.cjs` with `module.exports = require('./dist/esm-compat')` using `createRequire` to bridge ESM. Not ideal long-term but helpful.

alex: I'm going to open a GH issue to track SDK changes required for better test-runner parity (CJS wrappers, export map fixes, README test hints, and a sample app demonstrating Vitest/Jest configs).

maria-dev: Noted a concrete config that helped me in Vitest: 
```js
test: {
  environment: 'node',
  deps: { inline: ['@redwood-inference/sdk'] },
}
```
plus adding `type: 'module'` in package.json in the test project. But that doesn't help Jest.

katy: Also add docs: Vitest: use `deps.inline` + `resolve.alias` sample. Jest: `transformIgnorePatterns` to include SDK and `NODE_OPTIONS=--experimental-vm-modules` on CI (if you use Node >=16). And a recommendation to avoid deep ESM-only imports.

maria-dev: I tried `transformIgnorePatterns` as suggested: it removed the syntax error but then mocks (jest.mock) still didn't intercept named exports — probably because the module got evaluated before the mock. Using `jest.isolateModules` helped in a few tests.

samir: TL;DR: short-term workarounds for app/test teams: alias the SDK to a test shim or inline transform. Long-term SDK fix: publish CJS artifacts, update export map for deep imports, and add a `test-utils` entrypoint intended for mocking.

alex: Created issue #398 with checklist: (1) add cjs top-level build, (2) update exports map for common deep imports, (3) add README section + sample app for Vitest/Jest, (4) add a test-utils/mock entrypoint. Assigning to @alex.

ci-bot: Issue #398 created: "JS SDK: test runner ESM/CJS compatibility — vitest/jest mocking failures" — assigned @alex — https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/398 :ticket:

maria-dev: Sweet, thanks y'all. This was blocking onboarding for a few new engs. The alias workaround is ok for now. :relieved:

josh: If you can paste a minimal repro repo I can try to add a tiny failing test and a sample config to the SDK repo.

maria-dev: I'll put together a tiny repro and link in the issue. Appreciate it! :pray:
